models_evaluated: eight published lung cancer prediction models (logistic regression on clinical variables and radiologist nodule characterizations, single-time-point chest CT AI, longitudinal imaging AI, multimodal models)

links.outcome: Generalization of lung cancer prediction models across clinical settings and sites outside training distribution
links.effect: Eight models failed to generalize across clinical settings and sites; single-time-point CT AI performed well on screening nodules but not other settings; all models performed poorly on biopsied nodules.
links.quote: Eight lung cancer prediction models failed to generalize well across clinical settings and sites outside of their training distributions.

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the external validity and generalizability of eight published lung cancer prediction models across different clinical contexts and cohorts, addressing out-of-distribution performance without testing a specific operational guardrail or deployment practice.
